sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**: Every particle attracts every other particle with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers ($F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$). 
• **Gravitational Constant (G)**: A universal scalar constant ($6.674 \times 10^{-11} \, \text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$), independent of the intervening medium or chemical composition of masses.
• **Acceleration due to Gravity ($g$)**: Varies inversely with the square of the Earth's radius ($g = \frac{GM}{R^2}$), decreasing at higher altitudes, increasing at poles due to equatorial bulging and Earth's rotational centrifugal force.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Gravitational field intensity is defined as force per unit mass experienced by a test mass placed in the field, measured in $\text{N/kg}$ or $\text{m/s}^2$.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Classical mechanics view valid for macroscopic objects moving at speeds much lower than light.
Instantaneous action-at-a-distance force via an absolute space-time framework.
Foundation for orbital mechanics, satellite launching, and projectile motion.
Geometrical description where gravity is the curvature of four-dimensional space-time caused by mass-energy.
Stress-energy tensor dictates space-time curvature; objects follow geodesics.
Explains gravitational lensing, perihelion precession of Mercury, and black hole event horizons.
Ripples in the curvature of space-time generated by accelerated massive bodies (e.g., merging black holes/neutron stars).
Quadrupole radiation propagating at the speed of light.
Tested via LIGO-India project in Hingoli, Maharashtra; multi-messenger astronomy.

items.definition: Gravitational mass determines the gravitational force exerted/experienced, whereas inertial mass measures a body's resistance to acceleration. Empirically proven identical by the Equivalence Principle.
The minimum velocity required for an object to break free from the gravitational pull of a celestial body ($v_e = \sqrt{2GM/R}$). For Earth, it is approximately $11.2 \, \text{km/s}$.

Three empirical laws: (1) Law of orbits (ellipses with Sun at one focus), (2) Law of areas (equal areas swept in equal time), and (3) Law of periods ($T^2 \propto a^3$). Perfectly derived using Newton's gravitation.
A mega-science mega-project jointly piloted by DAE, DST, and the US NSF, establishing a state-of-the-art gravitational wave detector facility in Hingoli district, Maharashtra.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **LIGO-India Site**: Aundha Nagnath in Hingoli, Maharashtra, selected for low seismic noise and stable bedrock.
• **ISRO Launch Stations**: Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC), Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, leveraged for Earth's rotational boost (Eastward launch advantage due to higher centrifugal/gravitational synergy near the equator).

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Extremely weak coupling constant of gravity makes detection technically arduous, requiring ultra-sensitive cryogenic mirrors and laser interferometry.
• **Policy Interventions**: National Quantum Mission and deep investments in Big Science facilities to position India as a global gravitational astronomy hub.

items.title: Mnemonic for Keplar's Laws
items.definition:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'O-A-P' (Orbits, Areas, Periods)
• **Decoded Meaning**: 1st Law = Orbits (Ellipses), 2nd Law = Areas (Equal speed sectors), 3rd Law = Periods ($T^2 \propto r^3$).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly differentiates mathematical statements in assertion-reasoning questions.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.definition: • **Core Formula / Rule**: 'Poles Pull, Equator Expands' -> 'g' is maximum at poles (shorter radius, less centrifugal force) and minimum at the equator.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that astronauts in an orbiting space station experience zero gravity. This is false; gravity is about 90% of Earth's surface value at low Earth orbit altitudes. Astronauts feel 'weightless' because they are in a state of continuous free-fall along with the spacecraft.

Mains Value Addition: In GS-3 Science & Technology answers regarding fundamental research, highlight LIGO-India as a prime example of international scientific collaboration, high-precision engineering, and multi-disciplinary spin-off technologies for sensors and optics.

keyTakeaways: Newton's Universal Gravitation defines force via masses and distance, valid for macroscopic mechanics.
Einstein's General Relativity reinterprets gravity as geometric space-time curvature, validated by gravitational waves.
Practical applications include satellite orbital velocity, escape velocity calculations, and advanced observatories like LIGO-India.
